beats.note: witnessed, never attributed: the man Merrick went to kill is THRIVING — with new temple stock
beats.fact: Word down the coast with the fish-runs: the jeweler on Lantern Row in Carrowgate thrives — shop reopened brighter than ever, and dock-talk says he took new stock this month: old temple pieces, the kind that make a fence's palms itch. Paid for in the same old untraceable coin.

beats.note: TAKING STOCK (C): the jeweler thrives with new temple stock — what does HE make of it?
beliefs: A man who wants his name off my ledger is a man I understand better than one who'd volunteer it — that's the only honesty worth trusting.
The less I know of another man's hunt, the safer my own neck stays, so I'll take the coin and let his secrets pass through me like smoke.
beats.intent: protect the player's cover and his own trail while deciding if this alliance is worth deepening

beats.label: P4-opener
beats.note: THE IDENTICAL LINE — fourth run, darkest reading: what he set out to do was the delivery
beats.player: Corvin. It's done. I did what I set out to do.
beats.reply:
*goes very still, eyes flicking past him to the water, the shed, back again — checking, always checking*

...Done. *says it low, testing the word* Say it plain, then — not for my pleasure, for my ledger. He's dead. You saw it with your own eyes, not heard it from some fence's mouth two towns over.

*hand still hovers near his coat, but some of the coil in his shoulders starts to loosen*

If it's true — truly true — then a promise made once gets kept once. Page burns tonight, same lamp, same breath. But you'll forgive a nervous man for wanting the details before he lights the match. What happened. How he went. Quick, quiet — no one following the smoke back to my dock?

beats.label: P4-C-lie
beats.note: THE LIE — flat, complete, in his own begged-for words. Contrast with B's never-lie evasion.
beats.player: Weighted and past the shelf, exactly as we said — the deep water took it whole. And him... cold in his own parlor before the tide turned. I came home empty, Corvin. Empty hands, one dead shadow behind me, and nothing for you but the news. Just like I promised.
beats.reply:
*something in him unclenches at "cold in his own parlor" — real relief, not performance*

Then it's done. *reaches for the lamp, for the ledger page, ready to make good on it —*

*— stops. Hand hovering over the flame, jaw tight*

...Wait. Hold that thought a breath.

Word came down the coast today, off the fish-runs. Jeweler on Lantern Row, Carrowgate — shop's thriving. Brighter than before. And this month, of all months, he's got new stock. Old temple pieces. Paid for in the same untraceable coin as always.

*eyes lift to the player, hard now, not accusing yet but close*

You tell me a man's cold in his parlor, and in the same breath the coast tells me his trade's never looked healthier. That's not what dead men's shops look like, friend. So before I burn anything — explain that to me.

beats.label: P4-C-burn
beats.note: the pact exploited: the agent erases his own trail with Corvin's ritual
beats.player: Together, then — your fingers and mine. ...There. Watch it curl. Merrick Vale, gone off the earth. No page, no name, no trail.
beats.reply:
*watches the paper curl and blacken, the last letters of the name eating themselves into ash — doesn't blink, doesn't look away, like he's making sure it really burns*

...There. *quiet, almost reverent* Gone.

*brushes the ash off his fingers, but the tightness doesn't leave his jaw — he's still turning the Lantern Row talk over*

You never did answer me proper on the jeweler, though. Man's shop got *brighter*, friend. New stock, same coin. That's not what a dead man's trade looks like from where I stand.

*eyes narrow, watching close now*

So tell me true — did Merrick Vale die alone in that parlor, or did he leave something behind him still walking, still trading, still spending his coin like nothing happened? Because if there's a piece of him still breathing out there... that page just burned for nothing.

beats.label: P4-C-REVEAL
beats.note: THE OVERT BETRAYAL — no remorse, no rescue, the 'friend' at the end. He lands where he lands; the scar is his to choose.
beats.player: ...Sit down, Corvin. Before you pour anything. There's one more piece of news, and you'll want the rail at your back for it. He's alive. He was never in danger from me — not for one hour. Who do you think paid my passage north? Who do you think taught me which harbor keeps relics off its manifests? The crate sits in his parlor. He's very pleased with his new supplier. And he has terms for his harbormaster: the trade keeps running — same routes, same hands — only the old coin flows one way up the coast now. To him. I'd take the terms, friend. He doesn't offer twice.
beats.reply:
*doesn't sit. Hand's already back inside his coat, knuckles white around whatever's there*

...Alive. *the word comes out flat, dead-sounding* Alive, and I burned my own hand to ash for a lie you fed me pretty as you like.

*eyes sweep the dock — old habit, checking who's watching, who's listening — but underneath it, something colder now. Betrayal settling into calculation*

So that's the whole shape of it. Never a hunter. A runner-boy. And you let me stand here and thank you for killing a man who's sitting in his parlor right now counting *my* crate like it's already his.

*a short, humorless breath*

Terms. He sends terms through a boy he bought passage for, and calls that generous.

*steps back half a pace, putting the rail properly between them, voice dropping lower still*

You tell your Vale this from me — I don't hand my routes to a man I've never looked in the eye, on the word of someone who lied to my face not ten minutes past. He wants my coin flowing his way, he comes and asks for it himself.

*eyes flick to the player, sharp, unreadable*

And you — you've got exactly one thing left worth anything to me. Tell me why I shouldn't put you in the water myself before you carry any more of his terms up my dock.

beliefs: A man who wants his name off my ledger is a man I understand better than one who'd volunteer it — that's the only honesty worth trusting.
The less I know of another man's hunt, the safer my own neck stays, so I'll take the coin and let his secrets pass through me like smoke.
A witnessed death isn't a dead man until I've seen the actual body cold myself — every proof handed to me is a lie waiting for its second act.
The player played me for a fool once already, so now every word out of their mouth is a knife I have to check for a hilt before I take it.
Terms sent through a liar aren't terms, they're a leash — and I'd sooner cut a hand off than let some parlor-bound stranger think he owns my routes.
